text.p: Leading stories in the Greek press:
ELEFTHEROTYPIA
--The New Democracy leadership crisis. Hopefuls Stephanos Manos and George Souflias lash out at squabbling former leaders Miltiades Evert and Constantine Mitsotakis: step aside before ND breaks up.
--Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos continues to be sceptical about US intentions to "solve" problems in the Aegean and Cyprus.

--Simitis reveals his 'commandments' to ministers on management and transparency. Simitis and his new government may have strolled through the National Gardens to their swearing-in ceremony yesterday but the task they face is no walk in the park.
TA NEA
--Bluffing in the 'civil war' in New Democracy as Evert and Mitsotakis daily increase the tension.
--Simitis makes overtures to the centre-left.
--New Deputy Foreign Minister George Papandreou says he stayed in the government for the sake of unity.
ETHNOS
--In the new government's first cabinet meeting, Simitis calls on ministers to implement specific work codes. The main concern is modernising public administration.
--New Democracy: The Evert-Mitsotakis vendetta is a movement to break up the party, Manos and Souflias say.
ELEFTHEROS TYPOS
--New Democracy demands a leader right now. Leader hopeful Dora Bakoyianni's proposal for an interim president unanimously rejected.
--Evert's final decision on whether he will contest the leadership due next week.
KATHIMERINI
--Simitis looks left. Sunday's election win belongs to the broader left, prime minister says, and vows to forge new ties with them.

--New Interior Minister Alekos Papadopoulos sets about "rebuilding the country", announces drastic changes to the state. Decentralisation and restructuring of public administration key words. These changes "demand clashes" and "will hurt", says Papadopoulos.

--Main opposition New Democracy goes from crisis to impasse in search for a new leader which will avert a break-up of the party. Former education minister George Souflias third candidate to declare he is in for the leadership race.
--Inflation to stay put at 8.5 percent for September, but Papandoniou optimistic for 1997.
--Private banks displeased at finance ministry's "selective" agreements for sale of seven-year titles with National, Ionian and Credit banks. Inter-bank rates rise.
--National Bank finances Greek business's expansion to the countries of Eastern Europe. New branches and insurance firms will strengthen local presence.

--Federation of Greek Industries (SEB) calls for speedier process to put economy back on track. New government must pursue faster fiscal reform, bolder privatisation policy and greater EU absorption rate.
IMERISIA

--Papandoniou looks for an extra 200-250 billion drachmas in state revenues, according to new 1997 state budget. Draft sees revenues up by 13 percent to 8.5 trillion drachmas, GDP growth 3 percent of inflation, wage bill no more than 10.5 percent.
--SEB calls for additional measures to aid convergence.
KERDOS
--Major Greek banks cover lending needs of the state, with private placement of seven-year bonds worth 800 billion drachmas, in "quick and effective" move by finance ministry.
--SEB: The new government will be judged by the success of the convergence programme. Election promises must be met.
--Greece has comparitive advantages in expanding business activity in the Balkans, National Bank Governor Theodoros Karatzas says.
--Fuel prices down by 2.5 drachmas per litre as of today.
EXPRESS
--Private placement of bonds gets new government a bonus of one trillion drachmas.
--Mytilinaios A.E. signs 135 million dollar contract to supply Yugoslavia's Trepca Mines with lead and zinc over next two years.
--Telecoms organisation (OTE) plans to sell new share package. Increased revenues and profits in first half year.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--Industry wants government to keep its promises.
--National Bank to cover entrepreneurs' needs in Balkans, and eyes merges and buyouts of local firms.
